newsitem.title: USA: Clinton, Bruton urge IRA to observe ceasefire.
newsitem.headline: Clinton, Bruton urge IRA to observe ceasefire.

text.p: President Bill Clinton and Irish Prime Minister John Bruton urged IRA guerrillas to observe an immediate ceasefire as a way of moving Northern Ireland peace talks forward.
"We can't make peace until we end violence," Clinton told reporters as he and Bruton posed for pictures ahead of their Oval Office meeting.
Bruton said the Irish Republican Army should agree to a ceasefire now rather than wait for British elections because a new government in London could have a new policy toward Northern Ireland.
He said that "from every point of view" it would be better for the IRA to institute a ceasefire now to clear the way for its political wing, Sinn Fein, to have a seat at all-party peace talks.
"We believe there is a major window of opportunity now," Bruton said.
